objective: exhaust conventional selection mechanisms for the universal minimal axial-torsion coefficient

nodes.branch: ordinary unbroken symmetry distinguishes minimal and added contributions
nodes.result: both multiply the identical invariant operator, so any symmetry allowing the nonzero minimal term allows an arbitrary additive coefficient

nodes.branch: named discrete, chiral, family or compensator transformation forbids the operator
nodes.result: fermion number, chiral phase, charge conjugation, parity, compensator reversal, E6 and residual family transformations all retain the scalar operator or at least its identity flavor direction
for nonzero Yukawa coupling the one-loop equation has only eta=0 as a finite fixed point; for zero Yukawa all eta are marginal

nodes.branch: new UV grading or nonrenormalization theorem
nodes.blocker: no declared grading distinguishes the two parent invariants while preserving the minimal fermion action and controlling the compensator and E6 breaking thresholds

nodes.branch: interacting fixed point predicts a nonzero universal coefficient
nodes.blocker: no complete anomaly-free Spin(2,3)-matter beta functional, fixed-point solution, critical surface or threshold trajectory is available

scope: ordinary symmetry, named discrete and family transformations, parent compensator parity, and published perturbative RG selection of the minimal axial coefficient
decision: No conventional symmetry can distinguish additive contributions to the same allowed operator, and the standard one-loop RG does not fix the minimal value. Further reopening requires a new UV grading/nonrenormalization theorem or a fully specified interacting fixed point and matching trajectory.
